claims.title: Static normalization does not preserve remaining checking cost
claims.statement: The unchanged guarded DAG normalizer lowers static charge 14 to 12 while immutable-cache remaining charge rises 2 to 12; the cache-relative optimum is 1.
claims.scope: Additional cache cost contract, not a refutation of PT-07.

claims.title: Cache-cut minimum attainment and bounded new work
claims.statement: For a finite currently valid dependency-closed checked cache, adding zero-price exact-state macros reduces minimum remaining checking charge to inherited finite guarded whole-DAG compilation. An optimum expands with at most |J|2^|E| newly checked nodes plus cached nodes.
claims.scope: Fixed snapshot, support-only guards, compatible immutable identities, nonnegative fixed weights; effective comparison separately required.

claims.title: Pathwise postponement of passive successful checks
claims.statement: Under non-interference, non-informative successful checking and terminal reproducibility, every interleaved one-terminal-proof policy has an acquisition-then-check policy with identical acquisition history and pathwise no-greater charge.
claims.scope: Structural sufficient conditions, not a universal iff; physical timings and multiple valued intermediate deliverables excluded unless separately modeled.

claims.title: Revalidation-aware exact-state cache profile
claims.kind: inherited frontier specialization and new cache application
claims.statement: Under complete conjunctive dependency validity d(v) subset L, minimum dependency antichains per exact state exactly preserve all-L zero-price macro availability. Snapshot availability can agree while a rule withdrawal produces remaining prices 13 versus 1.
claims.scope: Coarsest macro-availability profile, not necessarily terminal-value quotient. Helper implements rule-local factors plus child unions, not arbitrary occurrence-specific dependencies.

claims.title: Finite-memory CIRS versus finite source sidecars
claims.kind: standard finite-chain corollary applied to source crosswalk
claims.statement: Under strictly positive CIRS laws, a time-homogeneous finite-memory common behavioral controller restores all hidden standards iff their good-action sets have nonempty intersection. CIRS can succeed with unbounded memory when that intersection is empty.
claims.scope: Counts every clock, archive, growing integer and persistent random state as memory; no hidden-model seed access; not a new general POMDP theorem.

claims.title: Rational likelihood arithmetic and actual Has representability
claims.statement: A common denominator makes CIRS likelihood comparison exact integer-weight comparison; fixed finite lookup, multiplication, comparison folds and bounded pointer updates are primitive recursive and inherit numeric original-Has realizability from inspected PR compiler interfaces.
claims.scope: No new literal Has controller module, Lean replay, host correspondence, probability-law theorem or calibrated physical observation stream.

claims.title: Model coupling and timed cost contract remain separate
claims.statement: Cache accounting does not permit independent worst-model selection at chance branches or dropping timing/outcome/state correlation. ET17 policy vectors and ET19 joint timing law retain their owners. PT28/29 literal probability results concern a distinct source-lowered observer contract.
claims.scope: No new robust Bellman theorem or claim that atomic defect prices proof checking.

ownership: New bridge claims separated from inherited mechanisms and ordinary corollaries; no field-wide priority or programme closure.
